intro: Missouri's most famous old tree stands alone in a field. The Big Tree near Columbia is a bur oak of three to four centuries, already about two hundred years old when Lewis and Clark came up the Missouri River in 1804 It has sat through lightning and the floods of 1993 and 1995, and it is tied as the national champion of its species. It stands on family farmland and is seen from the road. Kansas City's old trees are a different kind: the lawn of the Linda Hall Library is a registered arboretum, and its trees are catalogued by number. A double-flowered horse chestnut that never drops a conker stands there, beside a purple beech far from the cool woods it came from, and a hardy rubber tree whose torn leaves hang together on threads of latex.
